content.jointProblem: Where should script normalization occur in KlozuraPro’s PostgreSQL search pipeline—during indexing, querying, or both—to reduce cross-script search failures without degrading relevance or response time? The first experiment would compare these configurations against the current baseline on representative contract–query pairs, including mixed-script text and ambiguous transliterations, measuring known-document retrieval, precision, latency and index size.

rationale.text: Dragić has evaluated phoneme-based token canonicalization on Serbian legal retrieval data, providing directly relevant methods for testing cross-script contract search.

sources.quote: We evaluated the approach on a manually annotated gold standard of 4 200 query–document relevance pairs drawn from a legal corpus of 38 000 court decisions.

rationale.text: His research covers query-time transliteration expansion, offering an alternative to rebuilding the index around canonical tokens.

sources.quote: This paper studies the effect of automatically expanding queries with their transliteration variants before submission to an inverted index.

rationale.text: He has studied accuracy–latency trade-offs between deterministic and neural normalization, relevant to the company's response-time requirement.

sources.quote: We measure mean reciprocal rank, P@5, and end-to-end latency at the 50th, 90th, and 99th percentiles on a server cluster of four nodes.
The transformer-based normalizer achieves MRR of 0.68 but adds 47 ms at the 99th percentile.

rationale.text: His applied work includes normalization modules piloted in internal document search, including collections containing contracts.

sources.quote: Mala i srednja preduzeća u Srbiji čuvaju interne dokumente — ugovore, zapisnike, izveštaje — u mešovitom pismu bez konzistentne politike.

Ovaj rad opisuje iskustva iz tri pilot implementacije interne pretrage zasnovane na open-source pretražnom okviru dopunjenom modulom za normalizaciju pisma razvijenim u okviru naše istraživačke grupe.

constraints.text: The solution must handle mixed-script documents and ambiguous Latin-to-Cyrillic mappings, rather than assuming each document uses one script.

sources.quote: We want a solution that is robust enough to handle mixed-script documents, not just fully-Cyrillic or fully-Latin ones
there are edge cases where the same Latin sequence maps to different Cyrillic letters depending on dialect conventions.

constraints.text: The implementation must integrate with PostgreSQL full-text search and meet an agreed threshold for imperceptible search slowdown.

sources.quote: PostgreSQL with full-text search for document storage
does not slow down search response times noticeably.

constraints.text: Scope integration and evaluation to the task-specific limit of one backend engineer for up to six weeks; broader company capacity does not establish additional availability for this task.

sources.quote: We have one backend engineer who can work on this for up to six weeks.
with capacity for roughly one external project at a time alongside normal product development.

constraints.text: Keep the collaboration small and research-focused: Dragić reports two active projects and capacity for one smaller industrial contract or consultancy, not unrestricted software development.

sources.quote: Trenutno je angažovan na dva aktivna projekta, ali ima kapaciteta za jedan manji industrijski ugovor ili konsultantski angažman.
nije zainteresovan za opšte projekte razvoja softvera bez istraživačke komponente.

constraints.text: Establish a sufficiently large, well-defined Serbian evaluation corpus acceptable to the researcher, with access arrangements consistent with the company's internal security policy.

sources.quote: Dragić preferira saradnju s kompanijama koje imaju jasno definisan i dovoljno veliki tekstualni korpus na srpskom jeziku

risks: Published results on court decisions, news and other search frameworks do not validate performance on KlozuraPro contracts or PostgreSQL. The first experiment must test that transfer, including ranking regressions and production-like latency.
Canonicalization can conflate distinct tokens or mishandle foreign names, abbreviations and ambiguous sequences. Exception-focused relevance judgments are needed before enabling it broadly.
The reported one-in-five failure estimate comes from January 2024 logs; current prevalence and the proportion attributable specifically to script mismatch remain unverified.

Researcher start date and weekly availability are unknown. Corpus access, annotation effort, infrastructure limits and budget are also unknown and could prevent completion within the backend engineer's six-week window.
Index migration, exception maintenance or a neural fallback could exceed the small engagement's implementation and operational capacity.
questions: Can Dragić confirm a start date and weekly commitment compatible with the six-week backend-engineering window?

How many contracts and usable query logs are available, and can representative examples and relevance judgments be accessed under approved confidentiality, tenant-isolation and data-handling arrangements?
What are the current PostgreSQL version, text-search configuration, tokenization and morphological processing, index size, query load and reindexing constraints?
What numerical limits define acceptable p95/p99 latency overhead, index growth and relevance regression, and what reduction in verified cross-script failures would justify deployment?
Which ambiguous transliterations, foreign names, abbreviations and within-token script mixtures occur in actual contracts, and who can adjudicate correct matches for the first experiment?
What budget, legal-domain annotation support and ML-engineering time are committed, and what licensing and maintenance arrangements would apply to any reused research code?
